facts.text: On this date in 1532, Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa at Cajamarca — with 168 men against an army of 80,000. It remains history's most lopsided military conquest.
On this date in 1776, the Netherlands became the first foreign power to salute the American flag, when a Dutch fort in St. Eustatius fired a cannon response to the USS Andrew Doria.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire United States. Within 1,000 km of that circle sits roughly half of humanity.
Tokyo's greater metro area has more people than all of Canada — yet its violent crime rate is lower than that of Zurich, one of the world's wealthiest and most policed cities.

Lesotho, San Marino, and Uzbekistan are the only countries entirely surrounded by just one other country. Lesotho's host is South Africa; San Marino and Uzbekistan sit inside Italy and Central Asia respectively.
On this day in 1914, the Federal Reserve officially opened for business — created after the Panic of 1907 exposed the U.S. as the only major economy without a central bank.
On Nov 16, 1945, the Nuremberg trials began restructuring German war debt — IG Farben alone was split into BASF, Bayer, and Hoechst, three companies now worth over $100B combined.
The S&P 500 has historically risen in November more often than any other month, making it the single most reliably bullish calendar period in U.S. equity history.
Berkshire Hathaway was originally a failing textile mill. Warren Buffett later called buying it the worst investment of his life — he estimates the mistake cost him $200 billion.
The Dutch East India Company paid uninterrupted dividends for nearly 200 years. At its peak, its inflation-adjusted valuation exceeded that of every company on Earth today combined.

On this date in 1974, humanity sent its first deliberate message to the stars. The Arecibo transmission would take 25,000 years to reach its target cluster — and assumes the recipients can read binary.
Your bones are not static scaffolding. The entire human skeleton replaces itself roughly every decade through a continuous process of cellular demolition and rebuilding.
On this date in 1904, the first SOS-equivalent distress signal was proposed at the Berlin Radiotelegraphic Conference. CQD — not SOS — was the original code.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh approximately one billion tons on Earth.
Trees in a forest share resources through fungal networks in their roots, with larger trees actively subsidizing smaller, shaded seedlings — sometimes of entirely different species.
On this day in 1532, Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa with 168 men against 80,000 — a ransom of a room filled with gold followed, yet Atahualpa was executed anyway.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates the civilization Cortés destroyed by three centuries.
On this day in 1914, the Federal Reserve opened for business — America's central bank arrived 100 years after Napoleon's Banque de France and 220 years after the Bank of England.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, before the American Civil War, before the telephone, and 140 years before most offices actually got one.

On this day in 1849, Dostoevsky stood before a firing squad, was pardoned at the last second, and went on to write Crime and Punishment. He called the mock execution the most significant moment of his life.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Coined by John Koenig in 2012 for his Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows — a invented word so precise it feels ancient.
Apricity (n.): the warmth of sun in wintertime. From Latin apricus, meaning sun-drenched. Recorded in English since 1623, then quietly lost — a word that deserved to survive.
On this day in 1849, Dostoevsky stood before a firing squad in St. Petersburg. The execution was a staged mock punishment. The word 'reprieve' never felt so physical to anyone as it did to him.

Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word meaning the shared glance between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. Linguists cite it as one of the most succinct expressions of human awkwardness ever recorded.
On this day in 1914, the U.S. Federal Reserve opened. The word 'bank' traces to Italian banca — the bench medieval moneylenders overturned when insolvent, giving English the word 'bankrupt.'

On this date in 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had already burned over 1 million ETH since its August launch — permanently removing it from supply. Fee burning as monetary policy had arrived faster than almost anyone predicted.

On Nov 16, 2018, Bitcoin's civil war peaked: a hash war between Bitcoin ABC and Bitcoin SV split BCH into two chains. Craig Wright publicly threatened to 'kill' the opposing chain by dumping BTC to fund mining attacks.

Bitcoin's genesis block contains the headline 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not as metadata, but as the coinbase transaction input. Satoshi timestamped the entire project as a rebuke to fractional reserve banking.

The Ethereum contract that held $150M in The DAO hack funds sat untouched for 27 days before the attacker moved anything. The delay gave the community time to organize the fork — the hacker's patience arguably cost them everything.

Lightning Network payment channels are legally unbroadcast transactions held in mutual custody. At any moment, either party can close the channel by publishing the latest state — the network runs on cryptographic threat, not trust.

On this date in 2022, Meta released Galactica — a 120B-parameter model trained on scientific literature. It was pulled 72 hours later after researchers demonstrated it confidently fabricated citations and physics.
On this date in 2016, AlphaGo's paper appeared in Nature, revealing it had already defeated Fan Hui 5-0 in October — months before the world knew a machine had crossed that threshold.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed more electricity than 1,000 US households use in a year, yet the model weights compress to roughly 1TB — less than a modern video game install.
The first neural network to beat humans at ImageNet, AlexNet in 2012, ran on two consumer GTX 580 GPUs with 3GB VRAM each. Today's frontier models require that much memory per attention head.

Transformers were introduced in 2017 to solve machine translation. Within five years, the same architecture dominated image recognition, protein folding, code generation, and audio synthesis — an architectural monopoly with almost no precedent in CS history.
